small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune configs now that the safe ones compile: try `BLOCK_OC=128, BLOCK_SP=64, BLOCK_IC=32` at `num_warps=8, num_stages=3` and `BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_SP=128, BLOCK_IC=64` at `num_warps=8, num_stages=2`. With KH=KW=3 and POOL_K=2 the inner GEMM is repeated 36 times per tile so larger M/N tiles amortize the weight reloads.
- Hoist weight loads out of the pool loop: for fixed `(kh, kw, ic_start)` the weight tile is identical across all 4 pool positions. Restructure so the outer loops are `(kh, kw, ic_start)` accumulating into a `(BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SP_full)` accumulator that covers all `POOL_K*POOL_K` output positions in one tile, then pool-reduce after the conv. This cuts redundant `tl.load` on `w` by 4×.
- Pre-permute `conv.weight` to `(OC, KH, KW, IC)` once in `__init__` (register as buffer) instead of permuting+contiguous on every forward call.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an im2col-style GEMM with one program per `(N, OC tile, OH*OW tile pre-pool)`: compute the full conv output tile into registers/SMEM, then do the 2×2 max-pool reduction in-register before the Mish epilogue. This avoids the current scheme of recomputing the conv 4× per pooled output (once per pool position) — the current loop nest reloads `x` and recomputes `tl.dot` for every `(pi, pj)` even though weights are shared.
- Use NHWC layout end-to-end and tile along the channel-K axis with `BLOCK_K = IC` (IC=64 fits) so the K loop is a single iteration; this turns the inner kernel into a clean `BLOCK_M × BLOCK_N × 64` matmul per `(kh, kw)`, which Triton's MMA path handles much better than the current fragmented K loop.
- Consider fusing the bias+subtract+hardswish into the GEMM epilogue at the conv output (pre-pool), then a separate small kernel (or persistent grid) does pool+mish — but a single fused kernel is preferred if register pressure allows. Target: ~3× headroom remains on this 6.89ms kernel since the math is only ~140 GFLOPs.
